stem: After a hemodialysis session, the RN compares the client's postdialysis weight with the prescribed target (dry) weight. What is the primary purpose of this comparison?

options.A: Assess whether excess fluid removal has brought the client toward the intended volume status
options.B: Determine dialysis solute clearance without using laboratory data
options.C: Diagnose a change in nutritional status from this single treatment

rationale: NIDDK defines dry weight as the weight after hemodialysis has removed extra fluid and explains that controlling fluid intake helps the client remain at the proper dry weight. Hemodialysis removes excess fluid by ultrafiltration. Comparing the postdialysis weight with the target weight therefore helps assess the client's volume-management result. B is incorrect because solute clearance is not established from weight alone. C overinterprets a single treatment-related weight change, which is largely driven by fluid removal. D requires assessment of the access/dialysis circuit rather than body weight.
educational_objective: Use postdialysis weight relative to target dry weight as a clinical indicator of volume management and fluid removal during hemodialysis.
source_organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), NIH; National Library of Medicine — NCBI Bookshelf
source_document_title: Eating & Nutrition for Hemodialysis; Hemodialysis — StatPearls
source_version_date: Current NIDDK resource and StatPearls last updated 2026-02-15; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: NIDDK Eating & Nutrition for Hemodialysis > What is my dry weight?: dry weight is the weight after a hemodialysis session has removed all extra fluid. NCBI Hemodialysis > Anatomy and Physiology: ultrafiltration is movement of water across the membrane and is used to achieve fluid removal; session ultrafiltration should balance euvolemia and hemodynamic stability.
source_claim_supported: Target/dry weight represents the intended postdialysis volume state after excess fluid removal, so postdialysis weight is used to assess volume-management progress rather than solute clearance or access flow.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed page 14, Physiological Adaptation: manage care of a client receiving hemodialysis; monitor and respond to fluid/electrolyte-related complications.
correction_summary: Replaced a generic pre/post-weight recall item with a clinically precise target-weight interpretation scenario and corrected the blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Physiological Adaptation.
audit_findings: NIDDK directly defines target/dry weight after excess fluid removal; current NCBI hemodialysis source supports ultrafiltration for fluid removal. A uniquely interprets postdialysis weight correctly. B-D are distinct measures not derivable from weight. The item avoids claiming that weight difference alone exactly equals ultrafiltration volume or dictates a universal future goal. Blueprint matches NCSBN 2026 hemodialysis management. Independent adversarial second pass found no second answer, cueing, ambiguity or unsupported precision.
